annotations.proposed_function: Self-assembly and phase separation via multivalent interactions
annotations.evidence: Its disordered C-terminal low-complexity domain (LCD, residues 267–414), rich in glycine, glutamine/asparagine, and serine, bears features of a prion-like region and plays a central role in self-assembly of the protein and in the pathogenesis of neurodegenerative diseases [ 3, 4 ].
annotations.curator_note: Exact positions given (residues 267-414). Corresponds to canonical TDP-43 LCD.

annotations.proposed_function: Mediates liquid-liquid phase separation and micelle formation through self-assembly into droplets and nanoparticles
annotations.evidence: At 150 mM NaCl and 50 μM total protein, the unphosphorylated LCD rapidly assembled into a dense population of micron-scale fluorescent spherical droplets, already abundant within a few minutes of sample loading (Figure 3d ).
annotations.curator_note: Exact positions not provided; suggest UniProt canonical lookup for TDP-43 LCD coordinates.

annotations.evidence: Collectively, these results demonstrate that the phosphomimetic LCD variants 12D and 12DD reproduce the essential feature of phosphorylation-driven micellization, forming spherical micelles above a low-micromolar CMC with concentration-independent sizes, underscoring the role of C-terminal charge in redirecting self-organization.
annotations.curator_note: Qualitative mention only; exact residue coordinates not provided. Suggest UniProt canonical lookup for TDP-43 LCD boundaries.

annotations.proposed_function: Mediates protein-protein interactions and cluster/micelle formation
annotations.evidence: For reference, in a cluster containing 20 chains of TDP-43 LCD 12pS that means computing rij for 86 out of the ∼ 8.6 million pairs of residues.
annotations.curator_note: Exact residue boundaries for the LCD are not provided in the text; only qualitative mention of its role in cluster formation.
